rounds.text: Alchemist Corporation Ltd is demonstrating a powerful acceleration in its fundamentals, evidenced by a massive 193% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a staggering net profit increase of 560% year-on-year [E12, E44]. This operational momentum is translating into broader financial milestones, including a robust 31% compounded sales growth over 10 years that further scales to 62% over 5 years [E8, E9]. Market participation reflects this improving outlook, with share price growth accelerating from 26% over 5 years to 55% over the past year [E14, E16]. Furthermore, the company benefits from operating within a chemicals sector tailwind with a score of +0.56, where sector median profit growth sits at a strong 30.6% [E51, E54]. Promoters have shown steadfast confidence by holding a heavy 74.11% stake with zero dilution over recent periods [E30]. Conceded: [E6], [E7], [E27], [E32].

Alchemist Corporation Ltd is priced aggressively at a P/E of 67.2x and a steep price-to-book ratio of 27.21x while sitting 100% of the way up its 52-week range [E1, E2, E5]. This lofty valuation demands an unsustainable growth trajectory, especially when a discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 18 per share, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -102.2% [E32, E33]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today’s price requires a 25.8% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case expectation of 16.0% [E34]. The fundamental financial health underpins severe underlying risks, highlighted by a negative return on equity of -16.0%, a negative ROCE of -6.6%, and low historical median ROE figures hovering near zero [E6, E7, E17, E18]. Operational cash generation is entirely disconnected from reported accounting profits, as negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.38 Cr in March 2026 contrast with a cash conversion flag, compounded by a heavy debt-to-equity ratio of 5.43x where borrowings exceed net worth [E24, E25, E26, E27]. Conceded: [E8], compounded sales growth over 10 years is 31%.

Conceded: [E1, E2, E5, E32, E33, E34]. The bear's focus on high valuation multiples and DCF models ignores an active turnaround where recent profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 138%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform market expectations [E36]. Momentum is firmly supported by fundamental catalysts, including a massive 193% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a staggering net profit surge of 560% year-on-year [E12, E44]. Furthermore, long-term secular expansion remains intact through a stellar 31% compounded sales growth over 10 years, accelerating to 62% over 5 years [E8, E9]. This top-line momentum benefits directly from a robust macro backdrop, as the chemicals sector sits securely in a clear tailwind with a positive score of +0.56 [E51, E53]. Dismissing these improving results based on stale sentiment or historical metrics risks missing an active operational inflection [E52].

Conceded: [E12, E44]. While the bull points to recent profit acceleration and a sector tailwind score of +0.56 [E51], this momentum rests on a severely distressed financial foundation characterized by a negative ROCE of -6.6% [E6] and a negative ROE of -16.0% [E7]. The claim of an active operational inflection [E52] is directly contradicted by negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.38 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.38 Cr in Mar 2026 [E25, E26], exposing a complete disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation. Furthermore, the reliance on top-line historical metrics like 31% 10-year sales growth [E8] ignores severe structural vulnerabilities, including heavy debt exceeding net worth with a leverage ratio of 5.43x [E27], a low interest coverage ratio [E39], and alarming debtor collection periods stretching to 202 days [E42]. Finally, dismissing the quantitative valuation risk as stale sentiment [E52] is indefensible when today's price of ₹ 37 implies an aggressive 25.8% earnings growth rate [E34] atop a rich P/E of 67.2 [E1] and a 27.21x price-to-book multiple [E2].
